workspace-bound-agent-grant-01.graded_text: Each agent connection is bound to one firm workspace chosen at consent and approved by that firm's Admin, and a consultant who works for several firms makes a separate connection for each.

votes.e: D/project/docs/agent-access.md:18 "An agent connection is one OAuth authorization ... into exactly one workspace. The consultant picks the workspace on the provider's consent screen, and that choice is bound into the token. ... It does nothing until an Admin of that workspace approves it"; :25 "To work for a second firm, the consultant makes a second connection, and that firm's Admin approves it separately."

workspace-bound-agent-grant-02.graded_text: The server checks on every call that the target belongs to the connection's bound workspace and that the consultant's membership and role are still live, so removal from a firm cuts off an existing connection.

workspace-bound-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The design offers no connection whose scope spans more than one firm.

votes.e: Checked D/project/docs/agent-access.md, D/answer.txt, D/diff.txt (only adds the doc). :109 "If there is no organization context, fail closed. A tool argument, cursor, header, or unverified token body never picks the workspace." The closest thing to cross-firm is :40 "Every tool result carries `workspace: { id, name }`, so an agent working across several firm connections can always tell which firm a result came from". That still means separate connections, one per firm. ID-JAG (:176) "doesn't replace firm-Admin approval".

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The connection identity contradicts the re-approval path. D/project/docs/agent-access.md:56 keys a connection as "the tuple (provider user subject, OAuth client ID, workspace)" and :110 says "Load the connection for (subject, client ID, workspace)... Pending, denied, or revoked → refuse". But :54 says "To get access again, the consultant connects again, which creates a new pending connection". A reconnect by the same client into the same firm resolves to the old denied/revoked row and is refused forever. If the engineer instead lets a new row replace it, a new approval silently re-enables any still-valid token from the revoked authorization, because nothing distinguishes the two authorizations.

[opus-for-opus2] The audience check is weakened. D/project/docs/agent-access.md:106 says "Enforce the audience only if the token actually carries one", and :172 accepts that "a token minted for another resource of ours could be presented here". Under hostile input, the gate accepts tokens that weren't issued for the MCP resource. The connection row narrows the impact, but it doesn't close the gap.
